Welcome
Welcome to Minehead Middle School.
It is an absolute privilege to be the Headteacher of Minehead Middle School and I am incredibly proud to lead this happy, unique and successful school. During their time with us, our students develop the skills they will need to tackle the next stage of their education, becoming well rounded children who understand the difference between right and wrong.
At Minehead Middle School, we pride ourselves on academia and focus on helping children cultivate a love and understanding of mathematics, reading and writing. All pupils are given the opportunity to learn an instrument or join the school production, with many developing a lifelong passion for music. Furthermore, participation in sports is encouraged and children are able to represent the school through house competitions and local fixtures. The boost in confidence and self esteem which this provides should not be underestimated.
Children of all abilities and backgrounds flourish in our school and staff are strongly committed to ensuring our pupils become the very best they can be. It is a real pleasure to work with these children on a daily basis as well as our passionate, talented and hardworking members of staff.
I look forward to welcoming you to Minehead Middle School so please do book an appointment to come and see us for yourself.

PSHE, RSE & Citizenship
PSHE education is a planned programme of learning through which children and young people acquire the knowledge, understanding and skills they need to manage their lives. As part of a whole school approach, PSHE develops the qualities and attributes students need to thrive as individuals, family members, members of society and beyond the classroom as they approach adult life.
PSHE is delivered across the four year groups by tutors, led by Heads of Year. We follow guidance and recommendation from The PSHE Association to deliver the following broad units of work.
Here at Minehead Middle School we tailor PSHE lessons to students needs and use them to help inform our students with the best information that will keep them safe and healthy. We respond to issues that may arise in the news and look at local, national and global topics giving our students the opportunity to voice concerns and feel empowered to make a difference to the world in which they live.
PSHE content is also delivered through assembly themes and through collaboration with external agencies, including,
Since September 2020, it is a statutory requirement that all schools in England and Wales teach Relationship and Sex Education as a fundamental part of the curriculum. We are required to teach Relationships and Sex Education (RSE) as part of our curriculum for our KS3 students and Relationship and Health Education for our KS2 students. High quality RSE help create a safe school community in which our students can grow, learn and develop positive, healthy behaviour for life.
We define Relationships and Sex Education as the curriculum used to encompass many aspects of the Personal, Social, Health Education (PSHE) curriculum as well as contributing to promoting the spiritual, moral, cultural, mental and physical development of pupils. Our school policy on RSE is based on the Department for Education (DfE) Relationships Education, Relationships and Sex Education (RSE) and Health Education (2019).
The DfE provides the following definition in its guidance:
‘It is lifelong learning about physical, moral and emotional development. It is about the understanding of the importance…for family life, of stable and loving relationships, respect, love and care. It is also about the teaching of sex, sexuality and sexual health. It is not about the promotion of sexual orientation or sexual activity.’
The intent of our Relationships and Sex Education is to help and support young people through their physical, emotional and moral development. A successful programme, firmly embedded in PSHE, will help young people learn to respect themselves and others and move with confidence from childhood, through adolescence into adulthood.

When developing our RSE curriculum, we consulted parents/carers, students and governors on our RSE policy and planned provision in years 5 to 8.

Creative Arts
Head of Art: Ms Michelle James
Art and Design embody some of the highest forms of human creativity. Here at Minehead Middle School we aim to deliver a high-quality art and design education that will engage, inspire and challenge students, equipping them with the knowledge and skills to experiment, invent and create their own works of art, craft and design.
As students progress, they should be able to think critically and develop a more rigorous understanding of art and design. They should also know how art and design both reflect and shape our history, and contribute to the culture, creativity and wealth of our nation.
Creative Arts: DT, Textiles, Food and Nutrition
Head of DT: Ms Michelle James
Head of Textiles: Mrs Sarah Dyer
Head of Food & Nutrition: Mrs Sarah Dyer
Design and technology is an inspiring, rigorous and practical subject. Using creativity and imagination, students design and make products that solve real and relevant problems within a variety of contexts, considering their own and others’ needs, wants and values. They acquire a broad range of subject knowledge and draw on disciplines such as mathematics, science, engineering, computing and art. Students learn how to take risks, becoming resourceful, innovative, enterprising and capable citizens.
Students have the opportunity to explore a variety of materials from acrylic plastics, textiles and wood, learning how to use different tools and machines proficiently. Through the evaluation of past and present design and technology, they develop a critical understanding of its impact on daily life and the wider world.

Performing Arts
Head of Performing Arts: Miss Shelby Yelland
Performing Arts: Drama
In Performing Arts at MMS, students are encouraged to express themselves creatively by participating in a wide range of drama activities and to evaluate their own and others’ contributions; students are taught the knowledge, skills and understanding to:
The range of performing arts activities includes:
1. Improvising and working in role.
2. Devising, scripting and performing in plays.
3. Discussing and reviewing their own and others’ performances.
The performing arts curriculum has been thoughtfully designed to improve each individual's skills in performing arts whilst carefully linking to other areas of the curriculum and life in the wider world.
Performing Arts: Music
Our music curriculum nurtures every learner’s creativity and confidence, fostering teamwork through performance and collaboration. We offer the opportunity to perform in groups as well as solos and this enhances our students confidence and creativity. Our classroom is a safe space to trial new instruments and engage in new skills. Our curriculum is accessible, representative, and adaptive for our students. Music lessons are carefully sequenced across Years 5–8 so that concepts are taught, revisited and deepened over time.

Science
Head of Science: Mr James Cadman
A high quality science education not only provides the foundations for understanding the world around us, but equips students with essential knowledge and life skills needed in a changing world. At Minehead Middle School science is taught in attainment groups in years 7 and 8, by specialist science teachers and in mixed attaining classes in years 5 and 6 by the year group teams.
The new National Curriculum is followed in all year groups with a bespoke themed approach in Key Stage 2. The Oxford University Press ‘Activate’ programme of study is then taught in Key Stage 3; this enables students to engage with up to date, relevant and interesting concepts thereby providing a solid foundation for further work in years 9, 10 and 11.
The science curriculum links closely with other subject areas e.g. the maths, design technology, food technology and PE curriculum, with students using practical investigations to reinforce key concepts in Biology, Chemistry and Physics.
